metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code with a deployable entry point (Django WSGI app served via Apache/mod_wsgi) and a database dependency present. Single service with no IaC, no Dockerfile, but manual EC2 deployment confirmed in README. Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: Django app with PostgreSQL database performing CRUD operations on helpdesk tickets. Views expose read/search endpoints with database writes implied by the ticket lifecycle. Classified as stateful-crud.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.20 < 1.5 yields Not Ready band, but 11 High findings (upper boundary of 2-11 range) maps to Remediation Required tier. The divergence arises because this repository scores 1 on nearly every dimension — the overall score is extremely low while the High finding count is at the boundary of the Remediation Required range. The count-based tier (Remediation Required) is authoritative for classification.

findings.title: No Managed Compute — All workloads on raw EC2
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance (Ubuntu 12.04) with Apache 2.2 + mod_wsgi. No managed container orchestration, no serverless, no Fargate.
findings.gap: No managed compute services adopted. Single EC2 instance with no elasticity, no health checks, no automatic recovery.
findings.recommendation: Containerize the application and deploy to ECS/Fargate or EKS. Separate the database tier from the application tier.

findings.title: Self-Managed Database on EC2
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 is self-managed on the same EC2 instance as the application. Connection configured to localhost (127.0.0.1:5432).
findings.gap: Entirely self-managed database with manual patching, no automated failover, no PITR. Database co-located with application.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ deployment, automated backups, and PITR. Upgrade from PostgreSQL 9.1 to a supported version.

findings.title: No Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service detected. Ticket lifecycle management is entirely through inline view logic and raw SQL.
findings.gap: All workflow logic hardcoded in application code with no structured orchestration.
findings.recommendation: Introduce proper state machine patterns in application code. Evaluate Step Functions for multi-step ticket workflows as the system grows.

findings.title: No Async Messaging or Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. Email notifications are sent synchronously via SMTP. No SQS, SNS, EventBridge, or any message broker.
findings.gap: No async messaging for operations that would benefit — email notifications block request processing.
findings.recommendation: Introduce SQS or SNS for email notification delivery. Use EventBridge for ticket lifecycle events.

findings.title: No Network Security Configuration
findings.description: No network security configuration found. No VPC definitions, no security groups, no subnet configurations, no network segmentation.
findings.gap: No evidence of VPC with private subnets, security groups, or network segmentation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a custom VPC with private subnets for application and database tiers. Configure least-privilege security groups.

findings.title: No Managed API Entry Point
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or any managed entry point. Application served directly by Apache 2.2 with no throttling or request validation.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly via Apache with no managed entry point.
findings.recommendation: Place an ALB or API Gateway in front of the application. Configure health checks, throttling, and WAF rules.

findings.title: No Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configured. Single EC2 instance with static capacity.
findings.gap: All capacity is statically provisioned. No ability to respond to traffic spikes or scale down.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling when migrating to managed compute (ECS/EKS). Enable RDS storage auto-scaling.

findings.title: Minimal Backup — pg_dump Only
findings.description: A daily pg_dump cron job is the sole backup mechanism. No PITR, no automated retention, no restore testing, no cross-region replication.
findings.gap: Backup exists for main database only but lacks PITR, retention policies, and documented restore testing.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS with automated backups and PITR. Define retention policies. Document and test restore procedures.

findings.title: Zero Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC found. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Helm. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage. All infrastructure is ClickOps. Non-reproducible, non-auditable.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Terraform or CDK. Start with VPC/networking, compute (ECS), and database (RDS).

findings.title: No CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is entirely manual: SSH to server, git pull, restart Apache.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or deploy stages. No quality gates, no rollback.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline + CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) with build, test, security scan, and deploy stages.

findings.title: End-of-Life Language and Framework
findings.description: Python 2.7 (EOL January 2020) with Django 1.4 (EOL 2015). Both language runtime and framework are end-of-life with no security patches.
findings.gap: Language runtime and framework are both end-of-life. No security updates, limited cloud-native tooling support.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to Python 3.12+ with Django 4.2+ (LTS) or Django 5.x.

findings.title: Tightly-Coupled Monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries. Raw SQL in views, no separation of concerns, no service layer, no repository pattern.
findings.gap: No module boundaries, no defined interfaces, no data ownership separation. Business logic, data access, and presentation interleaved.
findings.recommendation: Modularize within the monolith: introduce Django apps with clean interfaces, use ORM, implement service/repository layer.

findings.title: All Communication Synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous HTTP. Email notifications sent synchronously via SMTP during request processing. No async patterns.
findings.gap: 100% synchronous communication. Email delivery blocks the HTTP request path.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async processing for email notifications using SQS or Celery. Decouple notification delivery from request path.

findings.title: No Async Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No background job framework, no async/polling patterns. Email sending blocks requests.
findings.gap: No async job processing for operations that may exceed 30 seconds.
findings.recommendation: Introduce background task processing (Celery with SQS, or Lambda for email). Implement status polling for batch operations.

findings.title: No API Versioning
findings.description: No API versioning strategy. No /v1/ URL patterns, no version headers, no versioning annotations.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes would be deployed directly with no backward compatibility.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (/v1/tickets/) when modernizing the API layer.

findings.title: All Endpoints Hardcoded
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded. Database on 127.0.0.1:5432, email server hardcoded as exchange.acme-corp.internal. No dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: All endpoints hardcoded in source code with no dynamic discovery or environment variable abstraction.
findings.recommendation: Externalize configuration to environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Adopt service discovery when decomposing.

findings.title: No Managed Object Storage
findings.description: Static files served from local disk. No S3 bucket for document or asset storage. No managed object storage or parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems with no managed storage, no redundancy, no accessibility.
findings.recommendation: Migrate static assets and file uploads to Amazon S3. Add CloudFront for delivery.

findings.title: Scattered Raw SQL — No Data Access Layer
findings.description: Raw SQL with string formatting scattered in view functions. No ORM usage despite Django providing one. No repository or DAO pattern.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered across views with no centralization, no abstraction, no consistent pattern.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Django ORM. Implement repository/service layer pattern. Remove all raw SQL string formatting.

findings.title: Database Engine Past EOL
findings.description: PostgreSQL 9.1 reached end-of-life November 2016 — over 8 years past EOL. No version pinning in IaC. No upgrade path defined.
findings.gap: Database engine 8+ years past EOL with no security patches and no version management.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to supported PostgreSQL version (15+) when migrating to RDS. Pin version in IaC.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configured. PostgreSQL data stored unencrypted on EC2 local disk. No KMS keys, no encrypted volumes.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for any data — database contents and static files stored in plaintext.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest on RDS with customer-managed KMS key. Enable S3 default encryption. Use encrypted EBS volumes.

findings.title: No API Authentication Enforcement
findings.description: No per-request authentication on view endpoints. AuthenticationMiddleware present but no views enforce authentication. Endpoints accessible without auth.
findings.gap: API endpoints effectively open. No authentication enforcement on any view. No token-based auth.
findings.recommendation: Add @login_required to all views immediately. Implement OAuth2/JWT when modernizing.

findings.title: No Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Django's built-in auth with no external identity provider. No Cognito, OIDC/SAML, SSO, or federation.
findings.gap: Application manages its own authentication entirely with no external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or corporate SAML/OIDC). Enable SSO.

findings.title: Hardcoded Secrets in Source Control
findings.description: Plaintext credentials committed to source control. SECRET_KEY and database password ('helpdesk2012') hardcoded in settings.py.
findings.gap: Critical: production secrets in plaintext in version control. Anyone with repo access has database credentials.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate all exposed credentials. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: No Compute Hardening or Patching
findings.description: Running on Ubuntu 12.04 (EOL) with Apache 2.2 (EOL). No SSM Patch Manager, no vulnerability scanning, no hardened images.
findings.gap: OS, web server, and all packages past EOL. No patching automation or vulnerability scanning.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported OS (Amazon Linux 2023). Implement SSM Patch Manager. Enable AWS Inspector.

findings.title: No Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. No SAST, no dependency scanning, no container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists to integrate tools into.
findings.gap: Zero security validation. Known vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded secrets) exist with no automated detection.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (Semgrep), dependency scanning (pip-audit), and secrets detection in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumented. No X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry. Only a Python 2 print statement in ticket_search.
findings.gap: No tracing. No ability to trace requests, identify bottlenecks, or diagnose failures.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with AWS X-Ray or OpenTelemetry when modernizing.

findings.title: No SLO Definitions
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No availability targets, latency targets, error budget tracking, or CloudWatch alarms.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for the helpdesk service. Implement CloudWatch alarms to track compliance.

findings.title: No Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business outcome tracking (ticket resolution time, volume, SLA compliance).
findings.gap: No business metrics — only default system metrics (if any). No visibility into business outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Implement custom CloudWatch metrics for key business outcomes: tickets created/resolved, mean time to resolution.

findings.title: No Anomaly Detection or Alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No CloudWatch alarms, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie. Failures detected only when users report them.
findings.gap: No alerting of any kind. Entirely reactive incident discovery.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for critical metrics. Add anomaly detection on error rates.

findings.title: No Integration Tests
findings.description: No integration tests. No test files found in repo. README mentions stale unit tests that are not present.
findings.gap: No automated tests at all. No regression safety net.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests for critical workflows. Run in CI pipeline.

findings.title: No Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms with owners, no CODEOWNERS file. Monitoring entirely absent.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is absent, not just unowned.
findings.recommendation: Establish monitoring ownership when implementing observability. Define CODEOWNERS for monitoring configs.
